Borderline Republic -- Immigration Entry Rule (posted notice, Ministry of Interior)
"Visa-exempt visitors may not be present in the country for more than 90 days within any
180-day period. To check compliance, count every day of presence within the 180 days
immediately preceding and including the last day of the trip being evaluated. Entry may be
refused, and departure may be flagged for review, if this limit would be exceeded."

Border control training memo (excerpt): "Officers should ask travelers approaching the
90-day mark to voluntarily provide their full travel history for the trailing 180 days if it
is not otherwise clear from passport stamps alone, since electronic entry/exit records for
land-border crossings from neighboring countries are not always complete. When in doubt,
request the traveler's own itinerary records rather than guessing from stamps alone."

Traveler 1 (Iveta Sokolova) -- entry/exit log, as provided to the border officer at her most
recent arrival:
Stay 1: October 1, 2025 - October 20, 2025 (20 days) -- purpose: visiting family
Stay 2: December 1, 2025 - December 31, 2025 (31 days) -- purpose: holiday travel
Stay 3: February 1, 2026 - February 15, 2026 (15 days) -- purpose: short business trip
Planned Stay 4: March 1, 2026 - March 25, 2026 (25 days) -- purpose: extended business trip,
  currently in progress at time of this review

Officer's note on Iveta's file: "Traveler proactively disclosed her full travel history when
asked, including the three prior stays above. Flagging Stay 4 for a compliance check given
how frequently she has been entering and exiting on the visa-exempt category over the past
several months. Awaiting confirmation on whether the planned March 25 departure keeps her
within the rolling limit."

Traveler 2 (Hendrik Voss) -- entry/exit log, as provided to the border officer:
Planned stay: February 1, 2026 - March 25, 2026 (this is Hendrik's only stay in the past
180 days; passport shows no other visa-exempt entries in the prior twelve months, and he has
not otherwise visited the country during that time).

Officer's note on Hendrik's file: "First visa-exempt entry in over a year based on passport
stamps; no compliance concerns apparent from the travel history provided. Noting for the
file in case a future review needs the baseline."

Consultant's email to Iveta, sent the day before her planned departure: "Just a reminder that
the 180-day lookback window is calculated ending on the LAST day of the trip being evaluated,
not on today's date if you were to leave early -- so if your plans change and you extend or
shorten the March trip, the whole calculation shifts. Let me know your final departure date
once it's confirmed so I can double check the math on my end as well before you go through
passport control."

Iveta's reply to the consultant: "Thanks for the reminder -- plan is still to fly out March
25 as booked, no changes so far. I did want to double check one thing though: does the time I
spent in the country back in 2024 count toward this at all, or does it fall outside any
possible 180-day window at this point? Just want to make sure I'm not missing something from
further back."

Consultant's reply: "Good question -- no, anything from 2024 is far outside even the widest
possible 180-day lookback from a March 2026 departure, so it's not relevant here at all. The
only stays that matter are the ones that actually fall within the 180 days immediately before
and including your last day in-country, which for a March 25 departure means counting back to
late September 2025. Everything before that point, including your 2024 travel, simply doesn't
enter into this particular calculation."

Border officer's final note, added at departure control on March 25, 2026: "Traveler
presented full itinerary voluntarily and departure proceeded without incident. Referring file
to compliance review team per standard procedure for any case flagged mid-stay, so the
180-day count can be verified against the officer's own log independently of the traveler's
self-reported dates before the file is closed."
